CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on evaluating the efficacy of the current treatment regimen and any necessary adjustments.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, expressing a continued overall improvement in his symptoms since his last visit. He reports that his sleep quality remains stable, with an average of 7-8 hours of sleep per night and only one nocturnal awakening. However, he still experiences difficulty with sleep onset after these awakenings, which he finds frustrating.
The patient notes that his tension-type headaches have decreased in frequency to approximately 1-2 times per week, with an intensity rated at 2-3 out of 10. He has been utilizing ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, reporting no side effects. Mr. Smith attributes this improvement to his ongoing commitment to physical activity and mindfulness practices, which he believes have positively influenced his mental and physical health.
Mr. Smith continues to actively participate in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions, which he finds beneficial. He has also maintained his bi-weekly acupuncture treatments, reporting that these sessions contribute significantly to his relaxation and stress management.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues his role as a software engineer and reports that he has successfully managed work-related stressors through effective time management and maintaining a healthy work-life balance. He remains active in his running group, which he finds valuable for both physical fitness and mental clarity. His dietary habits remain consistent, with adherence to a balanced diet, abstinence from alcohol, and limited caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Continued improvement in sleep quality; anxiety remains controlled; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Reduced headache frequency; intensity mild; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue shows slight improvement; no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/70 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-rested and engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed. Reinforce the importance of regular CBT attendance and mindfulness exercises to further enhance anxiety management. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Monitor sleep quality closely for any signs of regression. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Maintain amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Given the reduction in headache frequency, consider follow-up in two months to reassess. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to continue engaging in physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue does not further improve, consider referral to a sleep specialist for comprehensive evaluation.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-08-01 to continue monitoring symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
